Prior to the founding of the University of Cambridge in 1209, [Cambridge](/wiki/Cambridge "Cambridge") and the area surrounding it already had developed a scholarly and ecclesiastical reputation largely due to the intellectual and academic contributions of monks from the nearby [Ely Cathedral](/wiki/Ely_Cathedral "Ely Cathedral"). The founding of the university, however, mostly originated with an incident at the [University of Oxford](/wiki/University_of_Oxford "University of Oxford") during which two Oxford scholars, following the death of a local woman, were [hanged](/wiki/Hanging "Hanging") by the town's secular authorities. The local ecclesiastical authorities, who were not consulted, would have traditionally been inclined to pardon scholars in such cases. During this time, Oxford's town authorities were in conflict with [King John](/wiki/John,_King_of_England "John, King of England"). Fearing more violence from Oxford townsfolk, University of Oxford scholars began leaving Oxford for more hospitable cities, including Paris, [Reading](/wiki/Reading,_Berkshire "Reading, Berkshire"), and [Cambridge](/wiki/Cambridge "Cambridge"). Enough scholars ultimately took residence in Cambridge to form, along with the many scholars already there, the nucleus for the new university's formation.[[18]](#cite_note-Early_records-19)[[19]](#cite_note-20)[[20]](#cite_note-21)

By 1225, a chancellor of the university was appointed, and writs issued by [King Henry III](/wiki/Henry_III_of_England "Henry III of England") in 1231 established that rents in Cambridge were to be set *secundum consuetudinem universitatis*, according to the custom of the university, and established a panel of two masters and two townsmen to determine these. In 1949, [Venezuela](/wiki/United_States_of_Venezuela "United States of Venezuela") initiated the move towards the establishment of what would become OPEC, by inviting Iran, Iraq, Kuwait and Saudi Arabia to exchange views and explore avenues for more regular and closer communication among petroleum-exporting nations as the world recovered from [World War II](/wiki/World_War_II "World War II").[[39]](#cite_note-open-39) At the time, some of the world's largest [oil fields](/wiki/List_of_oil_fields "List of oil fields") were just entering production in the Middle East. The United States had established the [Interstate Oil Compact Commission](/wiki/Interstate_Oil_Compact_Commission "Interstate Oil Compact Commission") to join the [Texas Railroad Commission](/wiki/Texas_Railroad_Commission "Texas Railroad Commission") in limiting overproduction.[[40]](#cite_note-prize-40)

The US was simultaneously the world's largest producer and consumer of oil; the world market was dominated by a group of [multinational companies](/wiki/Multinational_companies "Multinational companies") known as the "[Seven Sisters](/wiki/Seven_Sisters_(oil_companies) "Seven Sisters (oil companies)")", five of which were headquartered in the US following the breakup of [John D. Rockefeller](/wiki/John_D._Rockefeller "John D. Rockefeller")'s original [Standard Oil](/wiki/Standard_Oil "Standard Oil") monopoly. Oil-exporting countries were eventually motivated to form OPEC as a counterweight to this concentration of political and [economic power](/wiki/Economic_power "Economic power").[[40]](#cite_note-prize-40)

There are more polysyllabic words in Mandarin than in all other major varieties of Chinese except [Shanghainese](/wiki/Shanghainese "Shanghainese"). This is partly because Mandarin has undergone many more sound changes than southern varieties of Chinese have, and needed to deal with many more [homophones](/wiki/Homophone "Homophone"). New words have been formed by adding [affixes](/wiki/Affix "Affix") such as *lao-* 老, *-zi* 子, *-(e)r* 儿/兒, and *-tou* 头/頭, or by compounding, e.g. by combining two words of similar meaning as in *cōngmáng* 匆忙, made from elements meaning 'hurried' and 'busy'.
A distinctive feature of southwestern Mandarin is its frequent use of noun [reduplication](/wiki/Reduplication "Reduplication"), which is hardly used in Beijing. In [Sichuan](/wiki/Sichuan "Sichuan"), one hears *bāobāo* 包包 'handbag' where Beijing uses *bāor*.
There are also a small number of words that have been polysyllabic since Old Chinese, such as *húdié* 蝴蝶 'butterfly'.

The singular [pronouns](/wiki/Pronoun "Pronoun") in Mandarin are *wǒ* [我](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%88%91#Chinese "wikt:我") 'I', *nǐ* [你](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E4%BD%A0#Chinese "wikt:你") 'you', *nín* [您](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%82%A8#Chinese "wikt:您") 'you (formal)', and *tā* ([他](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E4%BB%96#Chinese "wikt:他"), [她](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E5%A5%B9#Chinese "wikt:她") or [它](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E5%AE%83#Chinese "wikt:它")/[牠](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E7%89%A0#Chinese "wikt:牠"), 'he', 'she', 'it'), with *-men* 们/[們](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E5%80%91#Chinese "wikt:們") added for the plural. On May 19, the 76ers were awarded the third overall pick in the [2015 NBA draft](/wiki/2015_NBA_draft "2015 NBA draft"), where they selected [Duke](/wiki/Duke_Blue_Devils_men%27s_basketball "Duke Blue Devils men's basketball") center [Jahlil Okafor](/wiki/Jahlil_Okafor "Jahlil Okafor") with the third overall pick. The 76ers also signed [JP Tokoto](/wiki/JP_Tokoto "JP Tokoto") with the 58th overall pick. On November 27, the 76ers lost to the [Houston Rockets](/wiki/Houston_Rockets "Houston Rockets") 116–114, giving them a 27-game losing streak dating back to the previous season, which became the longest losing streak in professional sports. During the same game, the Sixers set a franchise record of 16 [three pointers](/wiki/Three_pointer "Three pointer") made during the losing effort. On December 1, the 76ers beat the Lakers at home by a score of 103–91, but not before setting a league record 28 consecutive losses dating to the 2014–15 season. In doing so, the 76ers also managed to avoid setting a new NBA record of most losses to begin a season. They instead tied the old record of 18 losses set by the then-[New Jersey Nets](/wiki/New_Jersey_Nets "New Jersey Nets") in the [2009–10 season](/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_New_Jersey_Nets_season "2009–10 New Jersey Nets season").[[71]](#cite_note-73)
